topics.description: A period of sectarian and political conflict centered in Northern Ireland and surrounding parts of Ireland from the late 1960s until the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this region, weapons such as the Armalite may have been smuggled using money from NORAID. The escalation of the dirty protests led to a hunger striker in this region’s Maze prison winning an election before dying the next month. Militants from this region bombed buildings such as the Baltic Exchange, the Old Bailey, and the Grand (*) Brighton Hotel. 26 people were shot in this region’s city of Derry on Bloody Sunday. In this region, the Troubles were ended by the Good Friday Agreement. For 10 points, name this region of the U.K. with its capital at Belfast.
parts.answer: Northern Ireland [prompt on U.K. or United Kingdom before “U.K.” with “What constituent country?”; reject “(Great) Britain”; prompt on “Ireland”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: On one particularly deadly day during this decades-long conflict, Lord Mountbatten was assassinated by a bomb planted on his boat and a convoy was ambushed at Warrenpoint. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this period of off-and-on sectarian violence and rioting that was largely ended by the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Troubles took place in cities like Derry, Belfast, and Dublin on this island, whose Northern region remains part of the United Kingdom.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In April 1916, a massive rebellion swept through Ireland and was brutally suppressed, with most of its leaders being executed. The rebellion began on the day after this major religious holiday, and thus became known as this holiday’s “Rising.”

topics.description: The political and social transformation in Japan beginning in 1868 that ended Tokugawa rule, restored imperial authority, and initiated rapid modernization.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This clan forced its nobles to send hostages to live in its capital in the “alternate attendance” system. This  clan defeated Ishida Mitsunari, who led the Toyotomi clan at Sekigahara. This clan adopted sakoku until the  arrival of the “black ships” of (*) Matthew Perry. This shogunate was overthrown during the Meiji Restoration.  For 10 points, name these isolationist rulers of the Edo period in Japan.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An editorial during this period titled “Leaving Asia” was written in response to the failed Gapsin coup. Forces opposed to the onset of this period were defeated in the Boshin War. Five principles for reform during this period were outlined in the Charter Oath. The (*) Satsuma Rebellion attempted to reverse the effects of this period nine years after its beginning. This period was prompted by the arrival of American “black ships” led by Commodore Matthew Perry. This period began after its eponymous emperor took power from the Tokugawa Shogunate. For 10 points, name this modernizing period of Japanese history.

topics.description: The Chinese imperial dynasty that ruled from 618 to 907 and is associated with territorial expansion, cultural prosperity, and poets such as Du Fu and Li Bai.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A consort from this dynasty claimed that she only needed an iron whip, an iron hammer, and a dagger to subdue a horse. The Silla kingdom sought this dynasty’s help in defeating Goguryeo, ending the Three Kingdoms of Korea period. A consort from this dynasty, (*) Yang Guifei, was put to death during a rebellion led by her adopted son. This dynasty was interrupted by the reign of the female emperor Wu Zetian. An Lushan led a rebellion during this dynasty, which succeeded the Sui. For 10 points, name this Chinese dynasty that ruled from 618 to 907 AD and saw the flourishing of poets like Du Fu and Li Bai.

topics.description: The Mongol-ruled Chinese dynasty founded by Kublai Khan that was overthrown by the Ming dynasty in 1368.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about Kublai Khan, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Kublai Khan founded this dynasty of China. Revolts by the Han majority led to this dynasty being replaced by the Ming Dynasty.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Kublai Khan received this traveler as a visitor to his court. While imprisoned, this Italian wrote a book describing the wonders of Kublai Khan’s court for Western audiences.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Kublai Khan’s mainland campaigns were largely successful, but his two invasions of Japan were each thwarted by typhoons, described in Japanese by this term, meaning “divine wind.”

topics.description: An armored combat vehicle, typically tracked and equipped for direct fire, developed during World War I and used extensively in World War II and later conflicts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Battle of Raseiniai saw the use of the KV model of this weapon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this weapon, other examples of which included the Panther and the Tiger models of Nazi Germany. The Molotov cocktail was originally designed to counter these weapons during the Winter War.
parts.answer: tanks [accept heavy tanks; accept armored tanks]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The KV and T-34 were some of the tanks used by this country as it fought Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front of World War II. This country was led by Joseph Stalin for the duration of the war.
parts.answer: Soviet Union [or Union of Soviet Socialist Republics; or U.S.S.R.; prompt on Russia]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This 1943 battle on the Eastern Front was the largest tank battle in history. This battle was codenamed Operation Citadel and included nearly one thousand German and Soviet tanks fighting at Prokhorovka.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The area between two of these structures was known as "no-man's land" because it was completely deserted and filled with mud. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these holes dug by soldiers for shelter from gunfire. A stalemate occurred in the Western Front of World War I because of a style of warfare named for these structures.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The introduction of these machines ended years of trench warfare in World War I, since they could shield soldiers from gunfire. Types of them such as the Panzer were used heavily in World War II.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Trench warfare in World War I began after this 1914 battle in France, fought at a namesake river. Thousands of Allied soldiers were transported in taxis to this battle, which marked the failure of Germany's Schlieffen Plan.

topics.description: Saudi-born founder and longtime leader of al-Qaeda, responsible for directing the organization until his death in a 2011 U.S. raid in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
aliases: Osama bin Mohammed bin Awad bin Laden

parts.label: L
parts.question: To become members of this force, candidates must pass BUD/S training at this force’s West Coast base in Coronado, California. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this primary special operations force of the U.S. Navy. This force’s name indicates their ability to fight on the seas, land, and in the air.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In 2011, SEAL Team Six carried out Operation Neptune Spear to take out this al-Qaeda terrorist, who was hiding in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This Navy SEAL became the deadliest sniper in U.S. military history during his service in the Iraq War. This man was the subject of the autobiography American Sniper.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1998, this group bombed American embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this terrorist organization whose ideology is outlined in the book Knights under the Prophet's  Banner by its longtime executive Ayman al-Zawahiri (AI-mun ahl zuh-WAH-huh-ree).

parts.label: B
parts.question: Al-Qaeda was headed by this son of a Yemeni-Saudi construction magnate until 2011, when he was  killed by Navy SEALs.
parts.answer: Osama bin Laden [Osama bin Mohammed bin Awad bin Laden]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Al-Qaeda claimed responsibility for the 2000 bombing of the USS Cole while it was docked in this  Middle Eastern city by a namesake gulf.

topics.description: Selim I was an Ottoman sultan who defeated the Safavids at Chaldiran and conquered the Mamluk Sultanate, including Egypt, greatly expanding the Ottoman Empire in the early 16th century.
aliases: Selim I of the Ottoman Empire

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire’s ruler Selim the Grim was the father of a man who would go on to expel the Knights Hospitaller from Rhodes. This empire was called the “Sick Man of Europe” before World War I, and it repurposed the Hagia Sophia as a mosque when it conquered (*) Constantinople in 1453. For ten points, what empire was ruled by Suleiman the Magnificent and would eventually be mostly replaced by Turkey?

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Nurbanu Sultan, the real power behind the Ottoman throne from 1574 to 1583:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Nurbanu was the mother of Murad III, the successor to a sultan with this name. The first sultan with this name defeated the Safavids at the Battle of Chaldiran and destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate to conquer Egypt.
parts.answer: Selim [accept Selim I or Selim the Grim or Selim II or Selim the Sot]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Nurbanu claimed to be from this polity, and she actively promoted policies benefiting this polity. The Ottomans took over the islands of Cyprus and Crete from this polity, which controlled them as part of the Stato da Mar.
parts.answer: Venice [accept Most Serene Republic of Venice or Venetian Republic]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Nurbanu commissioned Mimar Sinan to construct one of these buildings in the Uskudar district of Istanbul. The Hagia Sophia was converted into one of these Muslim religious buildings after the Fall of Constantinople.

topics.description: Libyan political leader and dictator who ruled Libya from 1969 until his overthrow and death during the 2011 Libyan Civil War and authored The Green Book.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Due to France’s support for Chad in the Toyota War, this man supported the bombing of a French airline’s Flight 772. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this leader of Libya and author of The Green Book who was killed in Sirte during Libya’s 2011 civil war.
parts.answer: Muammar Gaddafi [or Qaddafi or Kaddafi or Muammar Muhammad Abu Minyar al-Gaddafi]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Gaddafi accepted responsibility for the bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over this Scottish town. The Helsinki warning was received before that bombing named for this town.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] After Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground in this country, Gaddafi paid the American victims $150 million. Another act of terrorism saw this country’s PM Benazir Bhutto assassinated in 2007.
parts.answer: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader was humiliated in a conflict that saw opposing Chadian soldiers equip pickup trucks with anti-tank missiles, the Toyota War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this North African dictator from Sirte, who was overthrown in the 2011 Arab Spring. This dictator outlined his political philosophy in the Green Book and accepted responsibility for the Lockerbie Bombing.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Gaddafi led this North African country, which disputed the Aouzou Strip with its southern neighbor, Chad. The U.S. embassy in this country’s city of Benghazi was attacked in 2012.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Aouzou strip is rich in deposits of this element, which can be processed from yellowcake. This element’s 235 isotope is used in nuclear reactors.

topics.description: A confederation of Indigenous nations in the northeastern Woodlands, centered in present-day New York and governed according to the Great Law of Peace.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This group was targeted and nearly wiped out by a scorched earth expedition led by John Sullivan. Jigonsaseh (“JUH-gon-SA-zay”) founded this group with two men, including the “Great Peacemaker.” This group was supported by the Dutch and English against the French and Algonquians (“al-GUNG-kwee-uns”) during the (*) Beaver Wars. This group was governed under the Great Law of Peace and was led by Joseph Brant during the American Revolution. During the Revolutionary War, this group’s Tuscarora (“TUH-skuh-ROW-ruh”) and Oneida Nations split from the rest of the group to side with the Americans. For 10 points, the Seneca and Mohawk Nations were part of what confederation of six Native American tribes in upstate New York?
parts.answer: Iroquois Confederacy [or Haudenosaunee or Six Nations or Iroquois League or Five Nations; prompt on Mohawk or Cayuga or Seneca or Onondaga or Tuscarora or Oneida by asking “what larger confederation was that group a part of?”]

topics.description: A Central American country associated with Miguel Ángel Asturias’s El Señor Presidente, the Guatemalan Civil War, and the 1954 CIA-backed overthrow of President Jacobo Árbenz.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Due to the influence of companies selling this good, O. Henry described Honduras as a “republic” of it. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this fruit that was harvested across Central America by the United Fruit Company, which later became the company Chiquita.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This country’s president, Jacobo Arbenz, spearheaded land reforms that United Fruit disagreed with, so they lobbied the CIA to launch a coup in this country in Operation PBSUCCESS.
parts.answer: Republic of Guatemala [or Republica de Guatemala]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The authoritarian government the United States installed in Guatemala led a genocide against this ethnic group. This ethnic group established the former cities of Tikal and Chichen Itza.
parts.answer: Maya [or K’iche Mayans; or Mayan Empire]
